channel.title: SolidCraft Forge – SCPF API Reference
channel.description: Recent content in SCPF API Reference on SolidCraft Forge

item.title: Anchor
item.description:
Select component attachment references and cardinal directions.

Related guide

Use when

Use cardinal or corner anchors to attach reusable component occurrences, or combine cardinal values to identify Box edges/corners.

Limits

Anchor is the assembly/alignment vocabulary. Within-component feature placement normally uses Faces instead. INNER_BOTTOM has no direction vector and therefore cannot be used as a cardinal selector.

Members

  • CENTER = center
  • TOP = top
  • BOTTOM = bottom
  • LEFT = left
  • RIGHT = right
  • FRONT = front
  • BACK = back
  • FRONT_TOP_LEFT = front_top_left
  • FRONT_TOP_RIGHT = front_top_right
  • FRONT_BOTTOM_LEFT = front_bottom_left
  • FRONT_BOTTOM_RIGHT = front_bottom_right
  • BACK_TOP_LEFT = back_top_left
  • BACK_TOP_RIGHT = back_top_right
  • BACK_BOTTOM_LEFT = back_bottom_left
  • BACK_BOTTOM_RIGHT = back_bottom_right
  • INNER_BOTTOM = inner_bottom
  • UP = top
  • DOWN = bottom

Aliases

CENTER, TOP, BOTTOM, LEFT, RIGHT, FRONT, BACK

item.title: assembly
item.description:
Declare a reusable class that composes component occurrences.

Related guide

Signature 

assembly(cls)

Use when

Decorate a class when the class itself represents a reusable assembly or subassembly built from component occurrences and their relationships.

Limits

build() must return a component occurrence or Assembly. The decorator does not itself create grouping or attachment relationships; those come from the objects returned by build().

Parameters

  • cls — Model class whose build() returns a component occurrence or Assembly.

Example 

@assembly
class Frame:
pass

item.title: Assembly.anchor
item.description:
Return one named assembly-owned attachment datum.

Related guide

Signature 

Assembly.anchor(self, name)

Use when

A consumer needs the target/reference pair previously exposed with with_anchor() in order to create an attachment.

Limits

The name must resolve to exactly one assembly-owned anchor.

Parameters

  • name — Name previously registered with with_anchor().

Example 

mount = frame.anchor("front_mount")

item.title: Assembly.group
item.description:
Wrap these assembly occurrences in a real nested native component.

Related guide

Signature 

Assembly.group(self, name)

Use when

The collection should appear as one named subassembly/browser unit in SolidCraft.

Limits

Grouping changes native hierarchy, not placement or relationships. Use attach() for mechanical relationships between occurrences.

Parameters

  • name — Native subassembly/browser component name.

Example 

frame = (left + right).group("Frame")

item.title: Assembly.show_assembled
item.description:
Explicitly show the normal assembled placement.

Related guide

Signature 

Assembly.show_assembled(self)

item.title: Assembly.show_exploded
item.description:
Show one named exploded view after the assembly is built.

Related guide

Signature 

Assembly.show_exploded(self, name)

item.title: Assembly.with_anchor
item.description:
Expose one named attachment datum owned by this assembly.

Related guide

Signature 

Assembly.with_anchor(self, name, target, reference, *, offset=(0, 0))

Use when

A mounting/reference name belongs to the meaning of the larger assembly rather than to the generic reusable component itself.

Limits

target must already belong to this Assembly. with_anchor() exposes a reference; it does not create an attachment by itself.

Parameters

  • name — Public name for the assembly-owned attachment datum.
  • target — Component occurrence in this Assembly that owns the real attachment reference.
  • reference — Anchor, named component anchor, AnchorFrame or AnchorTopology on target.
  • offset — Optional in-plane (u, v) correction passed through when attaching, in mm.

Example 

frame = (left + right).with_anchor("front_mount", left, Anchor.FRONT_TOP_LEFT)

item.title: Assembly.with_exploded_view
item.description:
Add one native SolidCraft exploded presentation to this Assembly. Define exploded views after composing the final Assembly. Use either automatic scale mode or explicit occurrence translations.

Related guide

Signature 

Assembly.with_exploded_view(self, name, *, scale=None, moves=None)

item.title: attachment-references
item.description:
Use richer local or topology-backed datums when a standard Anchor is not enough.

Related guide

Members

AnchorFrame

Describe one local attachment point and orientation.

AnchorFrame(origin: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), z: tuple[float, float, float] | scpf.core.Anchor = <Anchor.TOP: 'top'>, x: tuple[float, float, float] | scpf.core.Anchor = <Anchor.RIGHT: 'right'>) -> None

AnchorTopology

Describe an attachment datum that follows native SolidCraft topology.

AnchorTopology(edge: tuple[float, float, float], on: tuple[float, float, float], corner: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, z: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, x: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None) -> None

item.title: Axis
item.description:
Select one of the native principal X, Y or Z axes.

Related guide

Use when

Use Axis for primitive orientation and supported patterns, for example Cylinder(…, axis=Axis.X) or a linear Hole pattern along Axis.Y.

Limits

Axis is a principal-axis selector, not an attachment reference and not an extrusion Direction.

Members

  • X = X
  • Y = Y
  • Z = Z

item.title: component
item.description:
Declare one reusable physical component definition.

Related guide

Signature 

component(cls=None, *, include=())

Use when

Decorate a model class whose build() result represents one reusable physical part. Child defaults stay fixed unless explicitly published with include=. Parent Parameter/Expression inputs remain symbolic.

Limits

build() must produce one Shape when reused as a component.

Parameters

  • cls — Model class whose build() returns one physical part. Omit when using @component(…) as a decorator factory.
  • include — Child default parameters to publish. Use names, “*”, or a mapping for renamed shared parameters.

Example 

@component(include=("inside_corner_radius",))
class CornerBracket:
pass

item.title: Depth
item.description:
Choose a supported feature-depth policy.

Related guide

Use when

Use Depth.THROUGH_ALL for features such as Hole that should pass completely through their target instead of using a fixed distance.

Limits

THROUGH_ALL is currently the only named depth policy.

Members

  • THROUGH_ALL = through_all

item.title: diagnostics
item.description:
Public diagnostics for invalid model intent and lost symbolic parameter dependencies.

Members

ModelError

Report unsupported or invalid CAD model intent.

ModelParameterWarning

Warn that an editable model parameter lost a native CAD dependency.

item.title: Edges
item.description:
Select edges for supported fillet and chamfer feature operations.

Related guide

Use when

Use Edges.VERTICAL for the vertical edges of a supported rectangular body. Use from_profile() for named profile segments and from_vertices() for extrusion-axis edges grown from named profile vertices.

Limits

Only the selectors implemented here are public. from_profile() currently supports sides=“both”; from_vertices() requires named Polygon2D vertices.

Members

  • VERTICAL = vertical

Lower-level entry points for compiling Shapes or trusted model source files.

Related guide

Members

compile_model

compile_model(shape: scpf.core.Shape, name: str) -> dict

run_script

Execute a trusted SCPF model source file and return its command document.

run_script(path: str | pathlib.Path) -> dict

item.title: Faces
item.description:
Select named planar faces for within-component feature operations.

Related guide

Use when

Pass a Faces value to operations such as Shape.on() and Shape.shell() to identify a surface of the target body.

Limits

The enum defines all six cardinal faces. Individual operations may support only a subset; Shape.on() currently accepts TOP and BOTTOM. Component assembly attachment uses Anchor instead.

Members

  • TOP = top
  • BOTTOM = bottom
  • LEFT = left
  • RIGHT = right
  • FRONT = front
  • BACK = back

item.title: Occurrence.attach
item.description:
Create a rigid or planar relationship from this occurrence to another component.

Related guide

Signature 

Occurrence.attach(self, target, *, parent=<Anchor.RIGHT: 'right'>, child=<Anchor.LEFT: 'left'>, offset=(0, 0), gap=0, angle=None, as_built=False)

Use when

Placement should be expressed semantically between component references, such as left face to right face or one mounting frame to another, rather than as a calculated global XYZ position.

Limits

The target must be another component occurrence. Supported standard anchors currently focus on rectangular component geometry; custom AnchorFrame/AnchorTopology references cover more specific datums. as_built=True requires all other relationship arguments to remain at their defaults.

Parameters

  • target — Parent component occurrence to attach to.
  • parent — Attachment reference on target. Defaults to Anchor.RIGHT.
  • child — Attachment reference on this occurrence. Defaults to Anchor.LEFT.
  • offset — In-plane (u, v) offset on the parent attachment plane, in mm. Defaults to (0, 0).
  • gap — Separation along the parent anchor normal, in mm. Defaults to 0.
  • angle — Optional joint rotation in degrees.
  • as_built — When True, keep the occurrences at their existing poses and create an as-built rigid joint.

Example 

right = right.attach(left, parent=Anchor.RIGHT, child=Anchor.LEFT, gap=2)

item.title: Occurrence.copy
item.description:
Create another occurrence of the same reusable definition.

Related guide

Signature 

Occurrence.copy(self, *, name=None, placement=None)

Use when

Reuse one component definition for another physical occurrence.

Limits

Attachment state is occurrence-specific and is not copied.

Parameters

  • name — Optional explicit Forge name for the new occurrence.
  • placement — Optional absolute Placement for the new occurrence. When omitted, the source placement is inherited.

Example 

right = left.copy(name="right", placement=Placement(x=160))

item.title: Occurrence.group
item.description:
Place this occurrence in a named native subassembly component.

Related guide

Signature 

Occurrence.group(self, name)

Use when

Give one occurrence a useful native browser/subassembly parent.

Limits

Grouping changes hierarchy only. It does not align, attach or otherwise create a mechanical relationship. One occurrence cannot belong to several different groups.

Parameters

  • name — Native group/subassembly name.

Example 

grouped = bracket.group("Mounting brackets")

item.title: Shape
item.description:
Store Forge geometry and feature operations before SolidCraft executes them.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape(kind: str, data: Any) -> None

Use when

Shape values are normally returned by constructors such as Box(), Cylinder(), Hole() and Sketch.extrude(), then transformed or combined with the supported Shape methods/operators.

Limits

Shape is only Forge’s description of the model. SolidCraft owns the final BRep and feature history; users normally do not instantiate Shape(kind, data) directly.

Parameters

  • kind — Forge node type. Public constructors set this; normal model code should not invent kind values.
  • data — Data stored for that node type. Public constructors and methods build this payload.

Example 

body = Box(80, 50, 12)

item.title: Shape.at
item.description:
Place a shape at absolute coordinates or align it to another Shape.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.at(self, x=0, y=0, z=0, *, anchor=<Anchor.CENTER: 'center'>, child=<Anchor.CENTER: 'center'>)

Use when

Use shape.at(x, y, z) for geometric placement. Box, Cylinder, Cone and Sphere support their documented anchors. Use shape.at(target) for the supported shape-to-shape CENTER alignment.

Limits

Shape-to-shape alignment currently supports CENTER-to-CENTER only. at() is geometric placement/alignment; selecting a support face for a feature is the job of Shape.on().

Parameters

  • x — Absolute X coordinate in mm, or a target Shape for shape-to-shape alignment.
  • y — Absolute Y coordinate in mm. Leave at 0 when x is a target Shape.
  • z — Absolute Z coordinate in mm. Leave at 0 when x is a target Shape.
  • anchor — Datum on this primitive that is placed at the requested coordinate. Defaults to Anchor.CENTER.
  • child — Child datum for shape-to-shape alignment. Currently only Anchor.CENTER is supported.

Example 

pin = Cylinder(d=8, h=20, axis=Axis.X).at(10, 0, 5, anchor=Anchor.LEFT)
centered = Sphere(5).at(body)

item.title: Shape.attach
item.description:
Anchor a supported feature explicitly to another Shape.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.attach(self, target, *, parent=<Anchor.TOP: 'top'>, child=<Anchor.BOTTOM: 'bottom'>, offset=(0, 0))

Use when

Use this lower-level feature-placement form when parent/child Anchor references are required explicitly.

Limits

This is legacy within-component feature anchoring. Prefer on() for simple face placement. It is separate from component occurrence attachment used by assemblies.

Parameters

  • target — Existing parent Shape that receives the feature.
  • parent — Anchor on the target Shape. Defaults to Anchor.TOP.
  • child — Anchor on the feature being placed. Defaults to Anchor.BOTTOM.
  • offset — In-plane (x, y) offset on the parent anchor surface, in mm. Defaults to (0, 0).

Example 

Boss(d=7, h=12).attach(case, parent=Anchor.INNER_BOTTOM, offset=(10, 10))

item.title: Shape.chamfer
item.description:
Chamfer selected solid edges by one equal distance.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.chamfer(self, distance, *, edges=<Edges.VERTICAL: 'vertical'>)

Use when

Bevel one or more edges of a supported feature-based body. Chamfer and fillet use the same edge-selection forms.

Limits

Edges.VERTICAL and cardinal Box edge selectors require a supported rectangular body. Named profile/vertex selectors require matching Polygon2D ids in a supported extrusion.

Parameters

  • distance — Chamfer distance in mm.
  • edges — Edge selection. Use Edges.VERTICAL, a supported two-direction Box edge selector such as FRONT + LEFT, Edges.from_profile(…), Edges.from_vertices(…) or a non-empty sequence of XYZ edge pick points. Defaults to Edges.VERTICAL.

Example 

body = Box(80, 50, 15)
bevelled = body.chamfer(3, edges=Edges.VERTICAL)

item.title: Shape.circular_pattern
item.description:
Pattern an existing native history feature around a fixed axis.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.circular_pattern(self, feature, *, count, axis=<Axis.Z: 'Z'>, angle=None, origin=None, alignment='right', reversed=False)

Use when

Repeat an already-created native feature around an axis while keeping one editable SolidCraft circular-pattern history feature, for example a Hole-based bolt circle.

Limits

The source feature must already be part of this Shape. Axis values cover principal or fixed XYZ axes. Native construction-axis, edge-axis and face-axis selectors are not exposed yet.

Parameters

  • feature — Existing applied feature Shape, or a non-empty sequence of applied feature Shapes. Forge resolves each source to its native history feature.
  • count — Total number of instances including the original. Use a positive integer or direct Parameter.
  • axis — Rotation axis as Axis.X/Y/Z or a non-zero fixed XYZ direction. Defaults to Axis.Z.
  • angle — Optional total pattern angle in degrees, as a fixed number or direct Parameter. Omit it for SolidCraft’s native 360-degree default.
  • origin — Optional XYZ point for a shifted fixed axis. With an Axis value and no origin, Forge emits the native principal-axis name directly.
  • alignment — Native alignment: “left”, “center” or “right”. Defaults to “right”.
  • reversed — Reverse the native pattern direction. Defaults to False.

Example 

flange.circular_pattern(bolt_cut, count=6, axis=Axis.Z)

item.title: Shape.contour_flange
item.description:
Create a native contour-flange sheet from an open Sketch chain. The receiver must be the Shape returned by Sketch.chain(…).finish(). Material dimensions define the sheet rule used by the new body; the contour feature itself receives only that rule name.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.contour_flange(self, *, distance, thickness, bend_radius, k_factor=0.5, rule_name='Forge Sheet', flip=False, reverse=False)

item.title: Shape.fillet
item.description:
Round selected solid edges with one radius.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.fillet(self, radius, *, edges=<Edges.VERTICAL: 'vertical'>)

Use when

Round one or more edges of a supported feature-based body. Fillet and chamfer use the same edge-selection forms.

Limits

Edges.VERTICAL and cardinal Box edge selectors require a supported rectangular body. Named profile/vertex selectors require matching Polygon2D ids in a supported extrusion.

Parameters

  • radius — Fillet radius in mm.
  • edges — Edge selection. Use Edges.VERTICAL, a supported two-direction Box edge selector such as FRONT + LEFT, Edges.from_profile(…), Edges.from_vertices(…) or a non-empty sequence of XYZ edge pick points. Defaults to Edges.VERTICAL.

Example 

body = Box(80, 50, 15)
rounded = body.fillet(3, edges=Edges.VERTICAL)

item.title: Shape.flange
item.description:
Add a native edge flange to existing sheet material.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.flange(self, *, edges, height, angle=90, height_from=None, position=None, flip=False)

Use when

Grow new sheet material from one or more existing sheet edges while inheriting thickness, K-factor and bend radius from the sheet rule.

Limits

This first slice accepts explicit fixed XYZ edge pick points only. Per-edge segment dictionaries, corner relief overrides, chained bends and radius overrides are intentionally not exposed.

Parameters

  • edges — Non-empty sequence of fixed XYZ pick points on sheet edges.
  • height — Positive flange height in mm.
  • angle — Bend angle in degrees. Defaults to 90.
  • height_from — Optional native height datum: “outer”, “inner” or “tangent”.
  • position — Optional native bend position: “inside”, “outside”, “middle”, “material_outside” or “tangent”.
  • flip — Reverse the flange side when True. Defaults to False.

item.title: Shape.fold
item.description:
Fold existing sheet material along one straight line.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.fold(self, *, line, angle=90, fixed=None, position='centerline', flip=False)

Use when

Bend material that already exists in a sheet blank. Dimensions and bend allowance come from the sheet’s shared rule.

Limits

This first qualified form supports one straight fold line. The line endpoints and fixed point are fixed finite coordinates.

Parameters

  • line — Two XY or XYZ points defining the fold line.
  • angle — Bend angle in degrees. Defaults to 90.
  • fixed — Optional XYZ point on the side that must stay fixed.
  • position — Native bend-line position: “centerline”, “start”, “end” or “mould”. Defaults to “centerline”.
  • flip — Fold to the opposite side when True. Defaults to False.

Example 

sheet.fold(
line=((20, -20), (20, 20)),
angle=90,
fixed=(-20, 0, 0),
)

item.title: Shape.hem
item.description:
Add a native hem to existing sheet material.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.hem(self, *, edges, length, gap=None, flip=False)

Use when

Fold one or more existing sheet edges back on the sheet while preserving native sheet-metal history and the inherited rule.

Limits

This first slice accepts explicit fixed XYZ edge pick points only. Generic edge selectors and compound hem profiles are intentionally outside this contract.

Parameters

  • edges — Non-empty sequence of fixed XYZ pick points on sheet edges.
  • length — Positive hem length in mm, measured to the outer face.
  • gap — Optional positive clearance in mm between the returned leg and the face it folds over. When omitted, SolidCraft uses the sheet rule.
  • flip — Reverse the hem side when True. Defaults to False.

item.title: Shape.on
item.description:
Place a supported within-component feature on a target face.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.on(self, target, *, face=<Faces.TOP: 'top'>, offset=(0, 0))

Use when

Put a Hole or another supported feature on an existing Shape and select its entry/support surface with Faces.

Limits

Shape.on() currently accepts Faces.TOP and Faces.BOTTOM. This is feature placement; component assembly attachment uses Anchor and the component occurrence attach() API.

Parameters

  • target — Existing Shape that receives the feature.
  • face — Target surface. Currently Faces.TOP or Faces.BOTTOM. Defaults to Faces.TOP.
  • offset — In-plane (x, y) offset from the target face centre, in mm. Defaults to (0, 0).

Example 

Hole(d=8).on(plate, face=Faces.TOP, offset=(20, 0))

item.title: Shape.path_flange
item.description:
Add a native path flange to existing sheet material.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.path_flange(self, *, edge, path, radius=None)

Use when

Create a multi-leg native flange from an existing sheet edge using one reusable open Sketch path.

Limits

The initial SolidCraft 0.45 contract accepts line-only open chains. Tangent arcs and generic edge selectors are intentionally rejected until the native path-flange runtime proves those contracts.

Parameters

  • edge — Fixed XYZ pick point on the existing sheet edge.
  • path — Finished open connected Sketch chain describing the flange path across that edge.
  • radius — Optional positive bend radius in mm. When omitted, SolidCraft inherits the active sheet rule.

item.title: Shape.perforate
item.description:
Add a native whole-sheet perforation field.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.perforate(self, *, diameter, pitch, margin=None, pattern='staggered')

Use when

Describe manufacturing perforations that belong to sheet flat-pattern, DXF and measured-volume semantics without cutting repeated B-rep holes.

Limits

This first slice covers the whole sheet only. Sketch/profile-bounded local perforation regions are intentionally outside the contract.

Parameters

  • diameter — Positive perforation diameter in mm.
  • pitch — Positive centre-to-centre perforation pitch in mm.
  • margin — Optional positive clear margin in mm. When omitted, SolidCraft uses the perforation diameter.
  • pattern — Native perforation layout: “staggered” or “square”. Defaults to “staggered”.

item.title: Shape.rectangular_pattern
item.description:
Pattern an existing native history feature in one or two directions.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.rectangular_pattern(self, feature, *, count, spacing, direction=<Axis.X: 'X'>, count2=None, spacing2=None, direction2=<Axis.Y: 'Y'>, alignment='right', alignment2='right', reversed=False, reversed2=False)

Use when

Repeat an already-created native feature while keeping one editable SolidCraft rectangular-pattern history feature.

Limits

The source feature must already be part of this Shape. Supplying a second direction requires both count2 and spacing2.

Parameters

  • feature — Existing applied feature Shape, or a non-empty sequence of applied feature Shapes. Forge resolves each source to its native history feature.
  • count — Number of instances in the first direction. Use a positive integer or direct Parameter.
  • spacing — Instance spacing in the first direction, in mm.
  • direction — First pattern direction as Axis.X/Y/Z or a non-zero XYZ vector. Defaults to Axis.X.
  • count2 — Optional instance count for the second direction.
  • spacing2 — Optional spacing for the second direction, in mm.
  • direction2 — Second pattern direction as Axis.X/Y/Z or a non-zero XYZ vector. Defaults to Axis.Y.
  • alignment — First-direction native alignment: “left”, “center” or “right”. Defaults to “right”.
  • alignment2 — Second-direction native alignment: “left”, “center” or “right”. Defaults to “right”.
  • reversed — Reverse the first native pattern direction. Defaults to False.
  • reversed2 — Reverse the second native pattern direction. Defaults to False.

Example 

plate.rectangular_pattern(cut, count=3, spacing=24, direction=Axis.X, count2=2, spacing2=28)

item.title: Shape.shell
item.description:
Hollow a supported solid and leave selected Faces open.

Related guide

Signature 

Shape.shell(self, thickness, *, open=<Faces.TOP: 'top'>)

Use when

Create an enclosure-like body with an even wall thickness while removing one or more named planar faces.

Limits

open= must be one Faces value or a non-empty sequence of Faces values. Support still depends on the underlying feature tree.

Parameters

  • thickness — Wall thickness in mm.
  • open — Face to remove, or a non-empty sequence of Faces values. Defaults to Faces.TOP.

Example 

Box(80, 50, 30).shell(2, open=Faces.TOP)

item.title: Sketch
item.description:
Create an explicit named 2D sketch scope.

Related guide

Signature 

Sketch(*, name='Profile', on=None, parent=<Anchor.TOP: 'top'>, plane=None, origin=None, offset=None, rotation=None)

Use when

Author one or more 2D profiles before creating a 3D extrusion. A Sketch may be standalone on XY/XZ/YZ or supported by an existing Shape.

Limits

Sketch(on=target) selects the body modified by the later extrusion. With the default parent=Anchor.TOP, Forge selects the largest +Z planar face at replay time. An explicit plane/origin bypasses face lookup. BOTTOM/CENTER relative placement still requires supported base metadata. offset remains a standalone-plane option. Leave the with-scope before extruding.

Parameters

  • name — Native sketch name. Defaults to “Profile”.
  • on — Optional existing Shape whose surface supports the sketch.
  • parent — Anchor selecting the supporting surface when on= is used. Defaults to Anchor.TOP.
  • plane — Explicit sketch plane: “XY”, “XZ” or “YZ”. Defaults to “XY” when on= is not used. With on=, an explicit plane is world-based while on= still selects the body modified by the extrusion.
  • origin — Optional explicit 3D origin for an explicit plane, in mm. May be used with on= when the Sketch should modify an existing body from a fixed world plane.
  • offset — Optional signed offset from a standalone origin plane, in mm.
  • rotation — Optional fixed (x, y, z) rotation in degrees for an explicit world-frame Sketch. Rotations are applied X, then Y, then Z.

Example 

with Sketch(name="Base", plane="XY") as sketch:
Rectangle2D(80, 50)

item.title: Sketch.add
item.description:
Add and place a supported 2D profile in this Sketch.

Related guide

Signature 

Sketch.add(self, profile, *, anchor=None, offset=(0, 0))

Use when

Add a profile explicitly or apply a deliberate sketch-local offset. Dimension-defined profiles default to semantic CENTER. Polygon2D, Text2D and native Slot profiles keep their authored coordinates.

Limits

Explicit Anchor.CENTER is supported for Circle2D, Rectangle2D and RoundedRectangle2D. Polygon2D, Text2D and native Slot profiles define their own sketch-local coordinates; leave anchor=None for those profile types.

Parameters

  • profile — Supported 2D Shape such as Rectangle2D, Circle2D, Polygon2D or a Slot constructor result.
  • anchor — Optional profile datum. Dimension-defined profiles default to Anchor.CENTER; coordinate-defined profiles keep their own coordinates.
  • offset — Sketch-local (u, v) displacement in mm. Defaults to (0, 0).

Example 

sketch.add(Circle2D(d=8), anchor=Anchor.CENTER, offset=(20, 0))

item.title: Sketch.extrude
item.description:
Extrude selected profiles from a completed Sketch.

Related guide

Signature 

Sketch.extrude(self, distance, *, sym=False, profiles=None, exact_regions=False)

Use when

Leave the Sketch context and create or cut material normal to the sketch plane. Use profiles= when the Sketch contains more closed regions than the extrusion should use.

Limits

A standalone Sketch requires a finite non-zero distance. Depth.THROUGH_ALL is only meaningful for a Sketch attached to an existing Shape and cannot be combined with sym=True. Profile pick points must be fixed finite numbers; Parameters and expressions are not accepted because SolidCraft 0.42 profile points are numeric.

Parameters

  • distance — Extrusion distance in mm, or Depth.THROUGH_ALL for an attached Sketch. Positive finite distances follow the plane normal; negative reverses it. THROUGH_ALL cuts through the attached target from the selected support face.
  • sym — When True, split a positive distance equally across both sides of the sketch plane. Defaults to False.
  • profiles — Optional non-empty sequence of fixed sketch-local (x, y) points. Each point selects the closed profile containing it. Leave None to extrude every profile.
  • exact_regions — When True, each profile point selects exactly the SolidCraft region containing that point. Only valid together with profiles=. Defaults to False.

Example 

cut = sketch.extrude(
Depth.THROUGH_ALL,
profiles=[(-30, 0), (-10, 0), (30, 0)],
exact_regions=True,
)

item.title: Sketch.mirror
item.description:
Mirror a profile or earlier Sketch result over the sketch X or Y axis.

Related guide

Signature 

Sketch.mirror(self, source, *, axis)

Use when

Create symmetric sketch geometry from a Circle, Slot, pattern result or earlier mirror result. The returned Sketch result contains the mirrored copies and may be used by a later supported Sketch operation.

Limits

The operation must be authored inside the active Sketch. Current native qualification covers attached Sketch(on=…) use. Only the sketch X and Y origin axes are supported. SolidCraft 0.42 stores the curves selected when the mirror is created. If an upstream pattern later creates extra curves after its count changes, those new curves are not added to that existing mirror automatically.

Parameters

  • source — A profile already in this Sketch, or a result returned by rectangular_pattern() or mirror() in the same Sketch.
  • axis — Mirror axis. Use Axis.X, Axis.Y, “x” or “y”.

Example 

with Sketch(name="Holes", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
circle = Circle2D(d=8)
sketch.mirror(circle, axis=Axis.Y)
with Sketch(name="Slots", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
slot = SlotCenterToCenter2D((0, 0), (20, 0), 8)
pair = sketch.rectangular_pattern(
slot, count=2, spacing=30, direction=Axis.X
)
sketch.mirror(pair, axis=Axis.X)

item.title: Sketch.rectangular_pattern
item.description:
Repeat a profile or earlier Sketch result with a native rectangular pattern.

Related guide

Signature 

Sketch.rectangular_pattern(self, source, *, count, spacing, direction=<Axis.X: 'X'>, count2=1, spacing2=None, direction2=None, alignment='right', alignment2='right', reversed=False, reversed2=False)

Use when

Repeat one Circle, Slot or other supported profile without drawing every copy separately. The returned Sketch result represents the source plus its copies and may be passed to mirror() or another supported Sketch operation.

Limits

The operation must be authored inside the active Sketch. Current native qualification covers attached Sketch(on=…) use. The two counts may create at most 500 instances in total. Per-instance suppression is not supported. SolidCraft 0.42 stores the curves selected by a mirror when that mirror is created. If a pattern later creates extra curves after its count changes, those new curves are not added to that existing mirror automatically.

Parameters

  • source — A profile already in this Sketch, or a result returned by rectangular_pattern() or mirror() in the same Sketch.
  • count — Number of instances in the first direction, including the original. Use a whole number from 1 to 500; a dimensionless Parameter may remain editable in SolidCraft.
  • spacing — Distance between instances in the first direction, in mm. A length Parameter may remain editable in SolidCraft.
  • direction — First sketch-local direction: Axis.X, Axis.Y or a fixed non-zero (x, y) vector. Defaults to Axis.X.
  • count2 — Number of instances in the second direction, including the original. Use a whole number from 1 to 500. Defaults to 1.
  • spacing2 — Optional distance between instances in the second direction, in mm. When omitted, SolidCraft uses the first spacing.
  • direction2 — Optional second sketch-local direction: Axis.X, Axis.Y or a fixed non-zero (x, y) vector. When omitted, SolidCraft uses the direction perpendicular to the first.
  • alignment — Position of the original along the first direction: “left”, “center” or “right”. Defaults to “right”.
  • alignment2 — Position of the original along the second direction: “left”, “center” or “right”. Defaults to “right”.
  • reversed — Reverse placement along the first direction. Defaults to False.
  • reversed2 — Reverse placement along the second direction. Defaults to False.

Example 

with Sketch(name="Holes", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
circle = Circle2D(d=8)
row = sketch.rectangular_pattern(
circle, count=4, spacing=25, direction=Axis.X
)
with Sketch(name="Slots", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
slot = SlotCenterToCenter2D((0, 0), (20, 0), 8)
pair = sketch.rectangular_pattern(
slot, count=2, spacing=30, direction=Axis.Y
)

item.title: Sketch.sheet_metal
item.description:
Create a native sheet-metal body from this closed flat Sketch.

Related guide

Signature 

Sketch.sheet_metal(self, *, thickness, bend_radius, k_factor=0.5, rule_name='Forge Sheet')

Use when

Start a fabricated sheet part from its flat blank before applying holes, folds, hems or other sheet-metal features.

Limits

The first qualified form requires one standalone XY Sketch with one closed profile. Leave the Sketch scope before creating the sheet.

Parameters

  • thickness — Sheet thickness in mm.
  • bend_radius — Default inside bend radius in mm.
  • k_factor — Neutral-axis K-factor. Must be greater than 0 and less than 1. Defaults to 0.5.
  • rule_name — Native SolidCraft sheet-rule name. Defaults to “Forge Sheet”.

Example 

with Sketch(name="Blank", plane="XY") as blank:
Rectangle2D(80, 40)
sheet = blank.sheet_metal(
thickness=2,
bend_radius=2,
k_factor=0.5,
)
